heroTitle: Business Bank Account Opening in UAE

whyNeededSection.title: Why You Need a Business Bank Account in UAE
whyNeededSection.subtitle: Without a corporate bank account, you cannot operate legally, accept payments, or stay compliant with UAE regulations.

items.title: Operate & Receive Payments
items.description: Required to accept payments, invoices, and trade legally with local or international clients.

items.title: Pay Staff via WPS
items.description: UAE law requires salary payments through WPS-linked accounts. No account means no compliant payroll.

items.title: Separate Business & Personal
items.description: Proper bookkeeping for VAT, accounting, and audits — essential for compliance.

items.title: Enable VAT & Tax Filings
items.description: Active corporate account is mandatory for FTA VAT registration and corporate tax returns.

items.title: Build Credit for Loans
items.description: Established banking history enables future financing, credit facilities, and trade finance.

items.title: Central Bank Compliance
items.description: UAE Central Bank requires all registered companies to operate with active corporate accounts.

eligibilitySection.title: Who Can Open a Corporate Bank Account?
eligibilitySection.subtitle: Multiple business types and individuals can open UAE corporate accounts.

items.title: UAE Mainland Businesses
items.description: LLCs, branches of foreign companies, and professional/civil companies registered with DED.

items.title: Free Zone Companies
items.description: All Free Zone licensed entities with valid business license — we match you with the right bank.

items.title: Offshore Companies
items.description: Allowed in select banks for non-trading purposes — holding assets and investments.

items.title: International Investors
items.description: Foreign investors with trade license, Emirates ID/residency, and notarized shareholder agreements.

items.title: E-commerce Providers
items.description: SaaS, dropshipping, digital marketing, and online businesses with valid Free Zone or Mainland license.

items.title: Freelancers
items.description: Permit holders from Dubai Media City, SHAMS, RAKEZ, twofour54, or Abu Dhabi Media Zone.

challengesSection.title: Bank Account Opening Challenges
challengesSection.subtitle: UAE banks have strict requirements — here's what can go wrong and how we fix it.

items.title: Strict KYC Verification
items.description: UAE banks perform deep KYC checks on business, owners, and source of funds. We prepare a complete KYC file that passes first time.

items.title: Enhanced Nationality Scrutiny
items.description: Certain nationalities and high-risk activities trigger extra vetting. We match you with banks aligned to your profile.

items.title: Proof of Local Presence
items.description: Banks often require Ejari, tenancy contract, or utility bill. We help you prepare these before applying.

items.title: Compliance Delays
items.description: Inconsistent documents can delay approval for weeks. Our pre-screened files avoid back-and-forth.

risksSection.title: Risks of Delaying Bank Account Setup
risksSection.subtitle: Waiting too long to open your UAE business bank account can cost you more than just time — it can halt operations, trigger penalties, and damage your business credibility.

warningCard.ctaMessage: Hi! I don't want to delay my bank account setup. Please help me get started.

items.title: Payment & Invoicing Delays
items.description: Without a corporate account, you cannot issue invoices, collect payments, or conduct B2B transactions — leading to cash flow problems.

items.title: VAT & WPS Issues
items.description: No bank account means no VAT registration, no WPS compliance, and possible fines from authorities for non-compliance.

items.title: Bad History Limits Financing
items.description: Even refused applications get recorded in compliance notes — making future loans and trade finance harder to acquire.

items.title: Fines for Inactive Businesses
items.description: Free Zone or Mainland authorities can penalize companies without active bank accounts — license suspension is possible.

risksSection.adviceText: Don't wait — bank account opening takes 2-20 days depending on type. The sooner you start, the sooner you can operate, receive payments, and stay compliant.

items.q: Can I open a UAE business bank account without residency?
items.a: Yes, non-residents can open corporate accounts — mainly for Free Zone or Offshore companies. Additional due diligence is required. We guide you through the compliant pathway and pre-screen applications.

items.q: How long does it take to open a corporate bank account?
items.a: Typically 5-20 business days depending on the bank, business profile, and shareholder nationality. Digital banks like WIO can be faster (2-5 days).
Trade license, MoA, passport copies, Emirates ID, proof of address, business plan, and KYC documents. We help prepare and verify everything.

items.q: Which UAE bank should I choose?
items.a: It depends on your business type, activity, and nationality. We match you with the most suitable bank — Emirates NBD, Mashreq, RAKBANK, FAB, ADIB, or WIO.

items.q: Can Free Zone companies open business bank accounts?
items.a: Yes — all Free Zone licensed companies can open accounts. We specialize in matching Free Zone businesses with suitable banks.

items.q: Do UAE business bank accounts support multi-currency?
items.a: Yes, most banks offer AED, USD, EUR, and GBP accounts with multi-currency features. We help you set up the right combination.

items.q: Can I open a zero-balance business account?
items.a: Some banks offer low or zero minimum balance accounts. We help find the best fit based on your business needs.

items.q: Can offshore companies open bank accounts in UAE?
items.a: Yes, offshore companies can open accounts in select banks for non-trading purposes only. We help with documentation and compliance.
